# MelloUI – An All-in-One UI for World of Warcraft: Forever

**Download:** [latest release](https://github.com/MelloCro/MelloUI/releases/latest) · [on CurseForge](https://www.curseforge.com/wow/addons/melloui) · [MelloUI Oldschool](https://www.curseforge.com/wow/addons/melloui-oldschool) (the painted skin) · **[Questie](https://www.curseforge.com/wow/addons/questie)** (needed for quests) · voice pack, optional: [part 1](https://github.com/MelloCro/MelloUI/releases/download/v0.18.3/MelloUI_VoicePack_Part1.zip) + [part 2](https://github.com/MelloCro/MelloUI/releases/download/v0.18.3/MelloUI_VoicePack_Part2.zip) · [changelog](https://github.com/MelloCro/MelloUI/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md)

**Discord:** [discord.gg/gdpQ6ep7bW](https://discord.gg/gdpQ6ep7bW) · help, bug reports and every new release

**Support:** [patreon.com/Mello_UI](https://www.patreon.com/Mello_UI) · MelloUI stays free; supporters get a thank-you role on the Discord

*Everything is a switch. On your first login the installer sets MelloUI up with you, fitted to your screen. Type `/mello` for the settings any time.*

## Install Questie too

**MelloUI's quests come from [Questie](https://www.curseforge.com/wow/addons/questie).** MelloUI keeps no quest data of its own any more. With Questie installed, its quests show on MelloUI's map and minimap in MelloUI's look, and the Quest List, Route to a quest and Dungeon Info's quests use them.

**Without Questie, no quests are shown.** The rest of MelloUI works as usual.

## MelloUI dresses the addons you already use

Your other addons do the work, MelloUI gives them its look and ties them into its map, tracker and route. They are all optional: install the ones you like and MelloUI finds them by itself. `/mello` > **Addons** lists each one, what MelloUI does with it, and a switch to leave it alone.

**Quests and leveling guides**

- **[Questie](https://www.curseforge.com/wow/addons/questie):** quests on the map, the minimap, the Quest List and Route, in MelloUI's look. Its tracker follows the Quest Tracker's settings.
- **[RestedXP Guide](https://www.curseforge.com/wow/addons/restedxp-guide), [Zygor Guides](https://zygorguides.com/), [Follow The Arrow](https://www.curseforge.com/wow/addons/follow-the-arrow), [Azeroth Pilot Reloaded](https://www.curseforge.com/wow/addons/azeroth-pilot-reloaded):** their steps on MelloUI's Quest Tracker, and Route leads you to each one.
- **[Polestar](https://github.com/fitzforge/polestar), [FlowUp](https://flowup-wow.com/), [TomTom](https://www.curseforge.com/wow/addons/tomtom), [Guidelime](https://www.curseforge.com/wow/addons/guidelime):** Route follows their steps, map pins or waypoints (Guidelime through TomTom's arrow).

**Map and minimap**

- **[RareScanner](https://www.curseforge.com/wow/addons/rarescanner):** rares, treasures and events on the map and minimap in MelloUI's icons, and the rares it finds on Rare Alert.
- **[HandyNotes: NPCs (Forever)](https://www.curseforge.com/wow/addons/handynotes-npcs-forever)** (with [HandyNotes](https://www.curseforge.com/wow/addons/handynotes)): the auction house, the bank, trainers, mount sellers and more on the map and minimap, in MelloUI's icons.
- **[GatherMate2](https://www.curseforge.com/wow/addons/gathermate2):** gathering nodes on the map and the minimap, each ore and herb in its own MelloUI icon. **[HandyNotes](https://www.curseforge.com/wow/addons/handynotes):** its notes on the map.
- **[NodeSight](https://www.curseforge.com/wow/addons/node-sight), [Lueur](https://www.curseforge.com/wow/addons/lueur):** the minimap stays in place while they scan for herbs and ore. Lueur's glow on the ore or herb you walk up to takes the place of MelloUI's gathering glints.

**Frames, bars and bags**

- **[Clique](https://www.curseforge.com/wow/addons/clique):** click-casting on MelloUI's unit and group frames.
- **[MaxDPS](https://www.curseforge.com/wow/addons/maxdps-rotation-helper):** spell recommendations on MelloUI's action bars.
- **[Offhand](https://offhand-wow.onrender.com/):** with two screens, MelloUI's animations and notices stay on the game's screen.
- **[Baganator](https://www.curseforge.com/wow/addons/baganator), [Bagnon](https://www.curseforge.com/wow/addons/bagnon), [ArkInventory](https://www.curseforge.com/wow/addons/ark-inventory), [BetterBags](https://www.curseforge.com/wow/addons/better-bags):** their bags in place of MelloUI's bag window, so B opens one bag window.
- **[AHledger](https://www.curseforge.com/wow/addons/ahledger):** auction prices in the Discard button.
- **[SharedMedia](https://www.curseforge.com/wow/addons/sharedmedia):** its fonts, bar textures and sounds in MelloUI's lists.

## The look

- **Three skins:** Default (the game's own look), Modern (MelloUI's own) and Oldschool (painted RPG art, a separate download).
- **Fonts, bar textures, colours and icons** in one place, and **Dark Mode** for the whole UI.
- **The game's windows** dressed to match, and a **Fader** that hides parts of the UI until you need them.

## Frames and bars

- **Unit frames** for you, your target, focus and pet, with a designer: click a part, drag it.
- **Party and raid frames** with indicators for heals, shields and debuffs.
- **Frame effects:** heals, shields, cooldowns and buffs land on the frames, and a halo shows who has aggro.
- **Personal Display:** your health, power and big cooldowns under your character, and a swing timer.
- **Nameplates** with threat colours by role, combo points, crowd control, quest marks and your debuffs; every part movable in a designer. Class medallions over your party; glints on herbs, veins and quest items.
- **Action bars, cast bar, XP and reputation bars,** and a **Level Up Card** with your gains and new spells at every level.
- **Minimap** with a Services row (the nearest repair, inn, flight master and more) and one tidy group for other addons' buttons.
- **Damage meter:** a race bar in fights, numbers on your frames and a fight history.

## Chat

- A cleaner chat with channel tabs, chat buttons and a whisper window.
- **Fake Link Warning:** a link dressed up as something else, like a Community invite written as an item, is marked FAKE LINK and opens nothing.

## Quests and travel

- **A world map of its own:** one seamless map with your quests (from Questie), party, route, dungeons and other addons' pins.
- **Quest Moments:** the game's yellow quest lines become small animations that fly to your quest in the tracker.
- **Route** finds the quickest way over roads and flights; an arrow and a marker in the world lead you.
- **Quest Tracker** and a **Quest List** of every quest near you (the Quest List needs Questie).
- **Dungeon Info:** every dungeon's bosses, loot and drop rates, with maps of Forever's own dungeons. Click a dungeon's entrance on the map to open its page.
- **Guide addons:** RestedXP, Zygor, Follow The Arrow, APR and TomTom steps show on the map, the marker and the tracker, with one arrow at a time.

## Quality of life

- Auto repair and junk selling, **Restock** for your supplies, quests accepted and handed in for you.
- **Reminders** for low supplies, mail, repairs, training and missing buffs.
- Bags sorted by kind, item quality gems, a junk Discard button and cooldown numbers.
- Combat text, gains beside your character, on-screen notices, quieter error messages, FPS and latency, and dark tooltips.

## Sound

- **Voice Over:** quest givers read their text aloud, with subtitles.
- **Custom Sounds** for clicks, windows and alerts, in each skin's style.

## And

- **Edit Layout:** move and size anything, the game's Edit Mode parts too. Your layout follows your screen's shape.
- **Profiles** to save, share and import your setup; each character keeps its own.
- **Gamepad:** MelloUI's windows, map, bags and action bars work with a controller in the game's Gamepad mode.
- The settings in English, German, French, Spanish, Portuguese, Russian, Chinese and Korean.

## Install

1. Download the [release zip](https://github.com/MelloCro/MelloUI/releases/latest) (not GitHub's "Source code" zip) and copy every folder in it into `World of Warcraft\_forever_\Interface\AddOns\`. Or install MelloUI with the CurseForge app.
2. **Install [Questie](https://www.curseforge.com/wow/addons/questie)** for quests, and any addon from the list above that you like.
3. Restart the game.

The voice pack's two parts unzip into the same `AddOns` folder; without it, the game's text-to-speech reads instead.

## Credits

- Parts of the configurator's design come from [EllesmereUI](https://www.curseforge.com/wow/addons/ellesmereui), used with its author's kind permission. Thank you!
- The maps of Forever's own dungeons (City of Dalaran, Ruins of Lordaeron, The Hall of Thanes, Excavation Site: Wetlands, The Drowned City, Krol'dok Stronghold, Alcaz Prison, Blackmaw Hold, The Shaper's Terrace) are by [Santiago Reyes](https://sreyesmaps.com/post/proyecto-atlas-de-azeroth-forever), from his "Atlas de Azeroth: Forever" project, used with his kind permission. Thank you! The other dungeon maps are Blizzard's own drawings from the game.
- Dungeon Info's Forever loot: [DungeonMaster](https://www.curseforge.com/wow/addons/dungeonmaster) by MalkDev (GPL-3.0). Drop rates: Data from [Everloot](https://everloot.app/), [CC BY-SA 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/).
- Classic quests, NPCs and drops: the [cmangos classic-db](https://github.com/cmangos/classic-db) (GPL-3.0); the data files made from it are GPL-3.0 too.

releases.notes:
- Map: on a battleground's map, hover a group member's dot to see who it is. Their name shows at the pointer in their class colour, and every name when several dots lie together, as on the game's own map.
- Quest Tracker: its scroll bar works with the mouse now. Drag the thumb or click the bar to scroll the list; it only showed where you were before.
- Chat: the Minimal chat view has a scroll bar at its right edge while a tab holds more lines than fit. Drag it to go back through the chat; the wheel works as before.
- Discard: hold Shift at a vendor and the button sells the cheapest stack of everything, also what it would keep because the auction pays more (with AHledger). The tooltip names what Shift would sell and follows the key.

- Nameplates: Class Coloured Player Names. Players' names on their nameplates in their class colour, with one switch for enemy players (Nameplates > Enemies, the Name part) and one for friendly players (Nameplates > Friendly players, the Name part). Both are off by default. NPCs keep the game's colours, and your own class colours from Look > Colours are used when you picked any.

- Nameplates: an enemy player's name no longer shows twice over itself after you target them (their first name over their full name). It happened with Show Names As on a short form and the name moved in the Nameplate Designer, and stayed until the plate left the screen.
- Nameplates: a name you hide in the Nameplate Designer is now hidden on players shown by a short name too, and the shade behind it goes with it.

- Combat Text: Healing Numbers look like healing now, not like a hit on your friend. A heal has a + before its number, swells in softly and floats up with a soft light in the healing colour behind it. No white flash, no streak and no shake, and a crit heal gets a ring of that light in place of the crit hit's effect.
- Combat Text: in a group, the numbers of your weapon swings no longer go missing after you healed someone.

- Combat Text: clearer names. Combat Text Style is now Personal Combat Text Style, and Your Damage is Combat Damage Style. The Text section has one size for each: Personal Combat Text Size (it was Text Around You, on Look > Fonts) and Combat Damage Size. Game Damage Numbers Size (it was Numbers Over Enemies) sizes the game's own numbers and no longer changes MelloUI's.
- Combat Text: Personal Combat Text Style has the same three new looks for the text around your character: Pop, Slam and Stamp, with an effect of their own for a crit you take and a crit heal. Lanes, Feed and Classic are still there.
- Combat Text: with Pop, Slam or Stamp each kind of line has its own area: Damage Taken, Healing, Procs and Resources. Edit Position (Quality of Life > Combat Text) opens Edit Layout with only these four: drag one to move it, use the wheel to size its text. They are not in the normal Edit Layout.
- Combat Text: Combat Damage Style is redone to land harder. Three new looks replace Rise, Beside, Fan and Stack: Pop (a hit lands above the plate with a hard pop), Slam (thrown out of the plate on an arc) and Stamp (a tidy column beside the plate). Hits are on screen about half as long. If you used Rise, Beside or Fan you now have Pop; Stack became Stamp.
- Combat Text: your crits have an effect of their own in each look: a flash with a ring and rays (Pop), a gold slash with sparks (Slam), a bar of light with a ring on the plate (Stamp). With Reduce Motion the number just appears and fades.
- Combat Text: Combat Damage In Groups (a test: try it and tell us how it goes). In a group MelloUI now shows your own hits in its look too, told from everyone else's by the game's combat log. It needs the Combat Log's filter on My actions, and your pet's hits are not shown in a group. Off: the game's own numbers in a group, as before.
- Combat Text: Healing Numbers. With a Combat Damage Style on, your heals show in the same look too, at the nameplate of the friend you heal, in place of the game's own healing numbers. It needs friendly nameplates shown and the Combat Log's filter on My actions. Where MelloUI cannot draw them (friendly nameplates off, or inside dungeons and raids, where the game keeps friendly nameplates to itself) the game's own healing numbers show as before.
- Combat Text: damage over time ticks are small and have a lane of their own at the plate's end, so they no longer crowd your hits.
- Combat Text: Number Outline (Thick, Thin or None) for your damage numbers. Thick is the default. None brings back the soft shade behind them.
- Combat Text: a spell's hit is in its school's colour: fire orange, frost blue, nature green, shadow violet, holy pale gold, arcane pink. Weapon hits stay white and their crits gold.
- Oldschool: the Borders tab is shorter. Nameplate Border and Level Orb are gone: your Frame Set draws the nameplates' frame and the level badge, so those two rows no longer changed what you see. The shortcut to the Minimap's Square Border is gone from that tab too; the setting itself is on the Minimap page.
